ChangedDecoders: Unsupported initial Data Matrix grid sizes skip allocation and cell sampling. The existing clock tracks resolve a supported size first, accepting either orientation of rectangles and DMRE. Supported initial estimates retain priority and clock alternatives remain available after failure. Perspective recovery, border/ECC/payload rules, budgets and public APIs remain unchanged. No production dependency is added.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 187/267 correct positive images versus 187/267 in the previous pass. Previously correct images lost: []; gained: []. Paired negative completion is [30, 30, 31, 30]/31 with the current binary and [30, 30, 30, 31]/31 with the previous qualified binary. All outcomes remain sensitive to shared-host contention and wall-clock budgets; no universal timeout or recognition advantage is established. Data Matrix avoids sampling dimensions that cannot decode, preserving clock-derived fractional-pitch recovery and supported-grid priority. Acceptance thresholds and configured budgets are unchanged. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. The invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracle and undeclared QR character encoding policies remain unchanged in scoring. Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported.

RegressionProof.Coverage: Fractional-pitch compatibility covers a supported but wrong initial estimate, an unsupported square estimate, a rotated rectangle and a rotated DMRE through simple, diagnostic, detailed and scanner APIs. Exact payloads and canonical symbol dimensions remain required. Existing damaged-clock original-grid priority, one-pixel modules, perspective, border/ECC and cancellation coverage remains.

BeforeChange.Limit: All four compatibility cases pass the unchanged decoder. They protect clock recovery against a naive unsupported-size rejection.

RegressionProof.HistoricalProof: Prior orientation, diagnostic and PDF417 remediation proof remains historical in previous-qualification.json. Current full suites and frozen/supplemental images are rerun.

TestExecution.Net472: Task-local runner configuration disables collection parallelism; recognition allowances and assertions are unchanged.
TestExecution.Limit: Short wall-clock allowances remain sensitive to shared-host load. Serial legacy qualification is not proof for default parallel execution.

SupplementalPdf417.Selection: All PNG images with UTF-8 text oracles in pdf417-1, pdf417-2 and pdf417-3, excluding the 18 frozen comparison images. The 38-image selection was fixed before the first supplemental outcomes. One revealed regression informed the final correction and permanent fixture; the final set is supplemental regression evidence, not an unseen holdout.
SupplementalPdf417.Limit: Supplemental images from the same upstream collection, outside the 18 frozen comparison images. The initial check exposed a sampling-priority regression that was repaired and added to permanent tests. This is regression evidence used during remediation, not an unseen holdout for the final candidate, a replacement ranking, or proof on an independent dataset. Wall-clock budgets also limit attribution of changed outcomes.

NegativeCostDiagnostics.Scope: Exploratory direct Data Matrix scans of three negative textures. Two warmups and six measured iterations per image, preloaded pixels, normal priority and CCD0 affinity. Previous host ran before current host; these are sequential shared-host diagnostics, separate from the rotated twelve-sample fair benchmarks.

QrPathDiagnostic.Scope: Exploratory three-iteration probe using the previous qualified binary on CCD0, normal priority, unchanged 1500 ms. The first iteration is cold. Direct single and all-QR calls and scanner paths have different search contexts and budgets. This is diagnostic evidence, not a replacement for frozen outcomes or a controlled comparison.
QrPathDiagnostic.Observation: Direct QR calls recover the expected payload; scanner outcomes vary. The QR search and nested-budget completion boundary require further investigation.
